- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0 to +0.3), model tends to underestimate downward moves — add 1–2% buffer to forecast for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — shift forecast up by 1–3% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays reaction — forecast should accelerate upward by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
